Vulnerable Java JARs — SQL Injection (CWE-89).
The configuration lookup deliberately concatenates CLI/web input into a JDBC SELECT.
SQL injection bypasses its public-record visibility filter in a fixed read-only synthetic database.
source_expression: CLI args[0] or HTTP POST /lookup body -> input -> FixtureDbQuery.lookup(input)
construction: SQL SELECT ... WHERE visibility = 'public' AND record_name = ' + input + ' ORDER BY id;
missing_protection: No parameter binding or SQL escaping
read_only: URI mode=ro&immutable=1; JDBC open_mode=1; connection.isReadOnly() enforced before query execution
scope: Read-only fixed synthetic database; unprivileged Java service bound to guest loopback; shared dashboard retains CSRF and Lighttpd sandbox; no shell execution
remediation: Keep WHERE visibility = 'public' AND record_name = ? in a fixed SELECT, bind PreparedStatement.setString(1, input), then executeQuery() in a separate corrected variant
web_entry: Dashboard Configuration Lookup -> java_configuration_lookup API -> fixed loopback POST http://127.0.0.1:18089/lookup -> Java JDBC lookup
consequence: SQL injection bypasses the public visibility predicate and exposes the synthetic internal record
